analyst_view.overall: Both sides have only 3 points: Feyenoord are 32nd and Porto 26th, and each needs points to reach the top 24. Feyenoord are in poor form under Giovanni van Bronckhorst, having lost 3-0 at home to Inter and 5-3 at Heerenveen. Anis Hadj Moussa, their most dangerous attacker, came back from Algeria duty injured and is a doubt; St. Juste and Bos have also been out. Porto have been solid in Portugal but are without Chris Smalling (knee) until the end of the year, which their recent form already reflects. Porto played a cup tie on 20 November and host Sporting five days after this game, so Farioli may rotate. No referee has been named.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals. Hadj Moussa, who carries most of Feyenoord's attack, is a doubt after picking up an injury with Algeria, and the numbers don't know that. Porto's sharp recent scoring and Feyenoord's leaky defence are already counted (+3% on Porto). I go slightly lower, to about 2.7.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.6 corners, with Feyenoord's slightly lower recent count already in (-3.5%). Nothing in the team news changes how either side gets the ball wide, so I stay at about 8.6.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.1 cards. Both sides need points, which can make a game scrappy, but the numbers already count their usual card rates and Porto's recent calm (-5%). No referee is named, so I stay at 4.1.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.5 shots and already add about 19% on Porto's side for how many shots Feyenoord have been conceding. Hadj Moussa's doubt and a possible Porto rotation before the Sporting game pull in opposite directions, so I stay at 27.5.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.0 shots on target, including a 15% boost for Porto from Feyenoord's poor recent defending. If Hadj Moussa misses out, Feyenoord lose their most accurate shooter, so I trim to about 9.7.
